column3: 2つ以上の人や物を比較するときに使う。
column4: This phone is cheaper than that one.||She is the best student in the class.||My town is as quiet as a village.
column5: 短い形容詞には-er / -est、長い形容詞にはmore / mostを使う。as ... asは同程度の比較に使う。
column6: This phone is more cheap than that one.||This phone is cheaper than that one.

column2: 可算名詞・不可算名詞と数量詞
column3: 量や数について話すときに使う。
column4: How much money do you need?||I have a few friends in Canada.||Would you like some tea?
column5: how muchは不可算名詞、how manyは可算名詞に使う。a fewは少数の可算名詞、someは肯定文などで使う。
column6: How many money do you need?||How much money do you need?

column3: 将来のこと、今決めたこと、予測、計画について話す。
column4: I'm hungry. I'll make you a sandwich.||We're going to visit Japan next month.||Look at the sky! It's going to rain.
column5: willはその場での決定や予測、be going toは既にある計画や目に見える根拠のある予測に使う。
column6: I going to visit Japan.||I'm going to visit Japan.

column3: 過去の特定時点で進行中だった行動、中断された行動、別の行動と同時に起きた行動を表す。
column4: I was cooking dinner at eight yesterday.||They were watching a film when the lights went out.||While I was walking home, it started to rain.
column5: was / wereと動詞の-ing形を使う。whenの後ろには短い出来事、whileの後ろには進行中の行動を置くことが多い。
column6: I cooking dinner at eight.||I was cooking dinner at eight.

column3: 義務、助言、禁止されていることについて話す。
column4: You should drink more water.||You mustn't smoke here.||You don't have to come if you're busy.
column5: mustは強い義務、shouldは助言、have toは必要性を表す。mustn'tはしてはいけない、don't have toはする必要がないという意味。
column6: You mustn't to smoke here.||You mustn't smoke here.

column3: 名詞の代わりに使ったり、物が誰のものかを示したりする。
column4: This is my bag. That one is yours.||Can you help me?||She made the cake herself.
column5: 主格、目的格、所有形、再帰形を文中の役割に応じて使い分ける。
column6: Can you help I?||Can you help me?

column2: 現在完了（過去形との違い）
column3: 経験、終わったばかりの行動、過去に始まり現在も続く状態、現在に結果がある過去の行動を表す。
column4: I have already finished my homework.||She has worked here since 2019.||Have you ever been to Korea?
column5: have / hasと過去分詞を使う。明確に終わった過去の時点を示す場合は通常、過去形を使う。
column6: I have finished it yesterday.||I finished it yesterday.

column3: 過去に始まり現在も続く行動、または終わったばかりで現在に結果がある行動を表す。
column4: I have been studying for two hours.||She has been working here since May.||It has been raining all morning.
column5: have / has beenと動詞の-ing形を使い、行動の継続時間や過程に焦点を置く。
column6: I have studying for two hours.||I have been studying for two hours.

column3: 将来の特定の時点で進行中となる行動を表す。
column4: This time tomorrow, I will be flying to Seoul.||At nine tonight, she will be working.||When you arrive, we will be waiting outside.
column5: will beと動詞の-ing形を使う。未来のある時点で進行中の行動を示す。
column6: I will flying tomorrow.||I will be flying tomorrow.

column3: 行動を受ける人や物が重要な場合、または行為者が不明・不要な場合に使う。
column4: This bridge was built in 1900.||English is spoken all over the world.||The meeting will be held on Monday.
column5: be動詞と過去分詞を使う。時制はbe動詞で示し、行為者を言う場合はbyを使う。
column6: This bridge built in 1900.||This bridge was built in 1900.
